summary: Unexpected 5xx spike from small-payload burst causing apigw connection queue lag and runtime FD exhaustion
description: Issue summary: Customers (BrightCart) observed a sharp rise in 5xx responses across API Gateway routes starting 2026-03-12 19:18 UTC during a short burst of small embedding requests. Impact: ~12% of requests from BrightCart returned 502/504 within a 7 minute window; other tenants in us-west-2 experienced elevated error rates (~1-2%). Environment: prod - us-west-2, Dedicated pool for BrightCart, API Gateway fronting realtime-proxy to serving runtime. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send concurrent embedding requests (payloads ~3-10 tokens) at ~900 rps from a single tenant connection affinity. 2) Observe keepalive reset cadence and rise in downstream runtime errors. Observed behavior: api-gateway shows accept-queue growth, connection queue lag, and frequent downstream connection resets. Runtime processes log "too many open files" and "ephemeral proxy fd exhausted" followed by short-lived process exits. Expected behavior: small-payload bursts should be absorbed by connection multiplexing and not cause fd exhaustion or upstream crashes. Logs/metrics: api-gateway accept_queue_length spiked to 650 (baseline 50), keepalive_reuse dropped to 18% from 92%, runtime FD usage reached 98% of ulimit, NV host metrics OK. Initial hypothesis: a combination of high concurrency with many short-lived connections and a regression in proxy keepalive handling caused file descriptor leak/exhaustion on the ephemeral proxy layer; this amplified backpressure to the serving runtime which triggers process evictions and 5xx propagation.
comments: 2026-03-12 19:25 UTC - Support (Janelle Park): Triage started. Collected BrightCart request IDs and asked customer to share a minimal repro. Notified SRE on-call.

2026-03-12 19:40 UTC - SRE (Marco Reyes): Observed abnormal accept-queue growth on edge nodes. Socket FD count trending to ulimit 65535 on two proxies. Reproduced locally with synthetic hammering script; confirmed fd leakage when connection churn >700 rps.

2026-03-12 20:05 UTC - Support (Janelle Park): BrightCart confirmed they rolled out a client change at 19:10 UTC that increased connection concurrency and reduced keepalive, which matches timing of the spike.

2026-03-13 01:12 UTC - Eng (Nia O'Connor): Added temporary guardrail patch to the proxy to increase FD soft limit for the process and rejected new connections past threshold. Deployed to a subset of edge hosts in us-west-2. Monitoring for reduction in 5xx.
2026-03-14 09:10 UTC - SRE (Marco Reyes): After patch, error rate for BrightCart reduced to baseline. Still seeing low-level keepalive reuse anomalies; follow-up planned to root cause leak path.
2026-03-14 12:05 UTC - Support (Janelle Park): Informed BrightCart of mitigation and recommended client-side keepalive tuning as immediate workaround. Customer acknowledged and requested postmortem.
investigation_notes: Edge diagnostics: High accept_queue_length correlated with specific edge host IDs. TCP retransmits rose ~3x during the spike window.
Proxy process: ulimit N of open files hit on two ephemeral proxies (pid 11422, 11423). Process restarts triggered by supervisor when FD count exceeded safety threshold.
Heap/Memory: Serving runtime memory and GPU metrics normal; not an OOM. Crash signatures point to unhandled error from accept() path, not model execution.

Reproduction: Local harness created to open many short-lived connections with small payloads. When keeping keepalive disabled, fd leak rate reproduces consistently. When using connection pooling, no leak observed.
Telemetry: Keepalive_reuse metric dropped prior to error spike; per-tenant connection churn spike matches BrightCart client deploy at 19:10 UTC.

Hypothesis refined: Regression in realtime-proxy introduced a path that incremented fd counter without closing on error path when upstream reset occurs, exacerbated by high churn of small requests. This leads to fd exhaustion which triggers process restarts and downstream 5xx.
Related artifacts: captured strace samples and /proc/fd listings for affected processes, linked in Confluence runbook. PR candidate identified in realtime-proxy.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied 2026-03-12 20:05 UTC: increased soft fd limit and added connection-throttle guard to reject new connections when fd usage > 90% to prevent crash-looping; this reduced blast radius while team prepared a proper fix.
Customer workaround recommended: use persistent connection pooling and enable keepalive; BrightCart reverted client change to reduce concurrency and confirmed error rate returned to baseline.

Root cause fix: Eng patch in realtime-proxy to close fd on accept error and to tighten error path cleanup (PR https://github.com/redwood/realtime-proxy/pull/512). Patch rolled to us-west-2 2026-03-13 03:20 UTC to canary hosts and then to full pool by 2026-03-13 06:00 UTC.

Post-deploy: monitoring shows accept_queue and FD usage returned to normal; no further runtime restarts observed. Eng to schedule a follow-up to add unit tests for accept-path and a metric to detect neglected fds.

Follow-ups: Add a support KB entry describing recommended client keepalive settings for small-payload high-concurrency embedding workloads; assign ENG-ops ticket to harden supervisor restart thresholds.
Status: Incident contained and mitigated; awaiting postmortem draft and customer-facing summary for BrightCart.
